title: Cherry Valley orchards from the air, 16 June 1938 — USDA aerial survey frame AXM-53-89

date.basis: Exposure date “6-16-38” is written on the frame itself, in the emulsion margin at upper left, alongside the frame number “AXM-53-89”. UCSB's index records 24 May 1938 as the BEGIN date of flight AXM_1938A as a whole; individual frames were exposed over following weeks, so the frame stamp is the authority for this image. Mid-June also places the frame at the end of the cherry harvest.

caption: Cherry Valley from directly overhead on 16 June 1938, in a U.S. Department of Agriculture aerial survey flown at 1:20,000. The valley floor is almost solid orchard — block after block of trees in tight rows, the planting that gave the place its name — threaded by the pale braided washes of Little San Gorgonio Creek and its tributaries running down from the north-east. Ranch headquarters sit in the middle of their own blocks, and the chaparral wall of the San Bernardino Mountain front closes the frame at upper right.
description: One 9×9-inch frame from flight AXM_1938A, a 1938 U.S. Department of Agriculture (Agricultural Adjustment Administration) aerial survey of Riverside County flown at a nominal scale of 1:20,000, so that each frame covers roughly 2.8 miles square. The frame centre is 33.9775 N, 116.9770 W, placing Cherry Valley squarely in the middle of the image. It records the community at its agricultural height: the orchard grid at its fullest extent before post-war subdivision, the section-line road network, isolated ranch complexes, the braided wash system draining the mountain front, and the abrupt boundary between irrigated valley floor and unimproved chaparral slope. Scanned at 5502×4328 px by the UCSB Library Geospatial Collection and released as a free download. Located 2026-07-24 while searching pre-war aerial coverage of the San Gorgonio Pass.
attribution: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Adjustment Administration — aerial survey flight AXM_1938A, frame 53-89. Scan courtesy UCSB Library Geospatial Collection.
caption_source: Frame margin annotations (date “6-16-38” and frame number “AXM-53-89”), plus UCSB Library FrameFinder flight metadata (FlightID AXM_1938A, Scale 20000, centre 33.9775/-116.9770).
rights_note: A 1938 U.S. Department of Agriculture (Agricultural Adjustment Administration) survey frame — a U.S. federal government work, public domain under 17 U.S.C. § 105 (catalog rights rule 3). UCSB Library scanned and distributes it free of charge and is credited as a courtesy, not as a rights holder; UCSB publishes no rights statement of its own for these scans. Caveat: 1930s AAA survey flights were commonly flown by contractors under federal contract, so public-domain status rests on the negatives having passed to the government as well as on § 105; no copyright notice or registration is known and the frames are distributed without restriction.
